source.title: Kyiv bridge hit in further Russian drone attack as German chancellor makes surprise visit
source.summary: Footage shows a drone hitting the Pivnichyi (Northern) Bridge as vehicles move across it, creating a large fireball.
source.evidence_text:
Footage shows a drone hitting the Pivnichyi (Northern) Bridge as vehicles move across it, creating a large fireball.
Video footage of Sunday's strike, verified by the BBC, shows cars moving on Pivnichnyi Bridge as a drone crashes into it before exploding, creating a ball of fire. A cloud of black smoke can be seen rising above the bridge.
Major bridges in Kyiv have been hit by Russian drone strikes for four consecutive days, as Moscow ramps up attacks on critical infrastructure in Ukraine's capital.
Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said two people were injured in the latest Russian attack. He earlier said that the Pivnichnyi Bridge's roadway was hit.
The latest attack came as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz made a surprise visit to Kyiv in a show of support against Russia's continuing full-scale invasion.
As emergency services responded to the incidents, Germany's Merz met Zelenksy in Kyiv. They laid wreaths to Ukrainian soldiers who have been killed in the war.
The two struck bridges are still standing - but the damage and restrictions to traffic and public transport have caused gridlock in parts of the capital at times.
Two people were injured when the Pivnichnyi (Northern) Bridge was struck on Sunday morning for the second day in a row, while the Pivdennyi (Southern) Bridge was hit multiple times earlier in the week.
Russia's military said it would be intensifying strikes on Kyiv and other Ukrainian regions. It earlier said it had hit the two bridges used to transfer Ukrainian troops.
Other videos and pictures have emerged on social media showing a gaping hole in the middle of a traffic lane on the bridge.
Kyiv's eight bridges across the wide Dnipro River link the western (right) and eastern (left) parts, and many of the capital's estimated three million residents rely heavily on the metro lines and trains to travel across the city.
"To get from the left bank to the right one and back - it's just hell," Kyiv resident Roman told the BBC on Sunday.
Large numbers of commuters cross the river, especially on weekdays. Repair teams are working to fix the damage and officials say they are planning temporary pontoon bridges, ferry services and even a tunnel under the river to keep Kyiv connected.
Klitschko also said a separate Russian drone strike had damaged a heating main, adding that there would be a temporary lack of hot water in the north-eastern Desnyanskyi district as a result.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenksy said on Sunday morning Russian drones had also attacked a warehouse in the north-eastern region of Sumy, killing one person.
Ukraine's Air Force said that overnight Russia had launched 135 drones, including 52 jet-powered ones. It said that 125 projectiles had been shot down.
Merz reaffirmed his country's support for Ukraine, writing on X: "Ukraine is facing decisive weeks. That is why I travelled to Kyiv today with the message: You can rely on us.
"Germany's security also depends on the outcome of this war. That is why we are helping out of our own self-interest as well."
Since Merz became chancellor in May 2025, Germany has become the single largest donor to Ukraine.
The Ukrainian president has made repeated appeals for Western allies to provide more military support to the country, including supplying advanced interceptors that can shoot down new jet-powered Russian drones and also ballistic missiles.
The Russian defence ministry said on Sunday it would intensify its strikes across Ukraine in response to comments made by Zelensky earlier this week, in which he said Kyiv would ramp up its attacks on Russian oil refineries.
The Russian foreign ministry on Saturday repeated a warning for foreign citizens, including diplomats, to leave Kyiv.
Responding to the warning, EU ambassador Katarína Mathernová wrote on X on Sunday: "The EU Delegation is staying. Threatening us will not stop Europe's support for Ukraine. It only reminds us why that support matters!"
German ambassador to Ukraine, Boris Ruge, reacted to Mathernova's post with: "Amen - we're staying".
Experts say Russian drones are unlikely to bring down the bridges - but repeated attacks will force their closure and risk weakening their structure, making them unusable.

discussion: The reading says traffic is difficult because of the damaged bridges. Why is it important for bridges to be open in a city?
If your city had damaged bridges, what problems might you have moving around? I think I would have problems with travel because it would be harder to get around.

grammar.explanation: We use the passive voice to talk about an action when we want to emphasize the object of the action or when the doer of the action is unknown or less important. The structure often uses a form of "to be" + the past participle of the main verb. For example, in news reports, the passive voice focuses on what happened, rather than who did it.
grammar.example_quote: Major bridges in Kyiv have been affected by Russian aerial vehicle strikes for four consecutive days.

They have been affected by Russian aerial vehicle strikes.

options: A diplomatic discussion.
A military attack or strike.
A public announcement.

Correct! "Affected" describes the impact of the strikes on the bridges' condition.
"by Russian aerial vehicle strikes" specifies the doer, but "affected" describes the bridges' state.

grammar.concept: Participle Clauses for Consequence or Simultaneous Action
grammar.explanation: Participle clauses, often introduced by a present participle (-ing form), are a sophisticated grammatical structure used to convey a consequence or result of the main action in a sentence. They can also indicate actions happening simultaneously with the main verb, offering a concise way to add detail and sophistication to sentences without relying on additional conjunctions. This usage is common in formal writing and news reporting for its efficiency and descriptive power.
grammar.example_quote: Video footage, independently verified, captured the moment an unmanned aerial vehicle crashed into the Pivnichyi Bridge as traffic moved across it, resulting in a large conflagration and a rising cloud of black smoke.

quiz.question: What is the primary focus of the news report?
options: The ongoing humanitarian crisis in Kyiv due to resource shortages.
The continued Russian aerial targeting of Kyiv's infrastructure and Germany's pledge of robust support.
The debate among experts regarding the structural integrity of Kyiv's major bridges.
option_feedback: Incorrect. While heating mains were damaged, the report's main theme centers on military attacks and diplomatic responses, not primarily humanitarian aid.
Correct. The report details both the Russian attacks on Kyiv's bridges and other infrastructure, and German Chancellor Merz's visit to reaffirm Germany's strong commitment to Ukraine.
Incorrect. Expert opinions on bridge integrity are mentioned but are a supporting detail, not the central theme of the entire report.

quiz.question: What consequences have resulted from the repeated attacks on Kyiv's bridges?
options: The complete collapse of the Pivnichyi and Pivdennyi bridges.
Widespread gridlock and temporary disruptions, despite the bridges remaining structurally intact.
A permanent cessation of public transport services across the Dnipro River.
option_feedback: Incorrect. The reading explicitly states that the "two targeted bridges remain structurally sound."
Correct. The article notes that the damage and traffic restrictions "have at times led to widespread gridlock," causing severe travel disruption for residents.
Incorrect. While there are disruptions, officials are exploring "contingency measures" like pontoon bridges and ferry services, indicating no permanent cessation.

quiz.question: In the sentence, "Moscow ramps up attacks on critical infrastructure," what does "ramps up" most closely mean?
options: Scales back
Intensifies
Diversifies
option_feedback: Incorrect. "Scales back" means to reduce, which is the opposite of "ramps up."
Correct. "Ramps up" signifies an increase in the amount or intensity of something, matching "intensifies."
Incorrect. "Diversifies" means to vary or expand the range, not necessarily to increase the intensity or volume of existing efforts.

quiz.question: Based on Chancellor Merz's statement, what is Germany's underlying motivation for assisting Ukraine?
options: A desire to gain political influence in Eastern Europe.
A belief that Germany's own security is intertwined with Ukraine's defense.
An obligation to demonstrate international solidarity as a major global power.
option_feedback: Incorrect. While political influence might be a byproduct, Merz's statement directly emphasizes "our own self-interest" in relation to Germany's security, not specifically political gain.
Correct. Merz explicitly stated, "'Germany's security also depends on the outcome of this war. That is why we are helping out of our own self-interest as well.'"
Incorrect. While solidarity is a factor, Merz's quote highlights "self-interest" as a core reason, suggesting a more direct link to Germany's national security rather than just a general obligation.

quiz.question: How did EU and German ambassadors respond to Russia's warning for foreign nationals to leave Kyiv?
options: They departed immediately, citing safety concerns.
They expressed concerns but stated their intent to remain in Kyiv.
They issued a joint declaration condemning the warning as unlawful.
option_feedback: Incorrect. Both ambassadors explicitly stated their intention to remain in Kyiv, directly contradicting the idea of departure.
Correct. Both Ambassador Mathernová and Ambassador Ruge affirmed their continued presence, with Mathernová stating the EU Delegation is staying despite the threat, and Ruge echoing 'we're staying'.
Incorrect. While they dismissed the warning, the text does not describe them issuing a formal declaration condemning it as unlawful.

quiz.question: In the context of the reading, what does "benefactor" refer to regarding Germany's role for Ukraine?
options: A military advisor.
A financial supporter.
A strategic ally.
option_feedback: Incorrect. While Germany provides military aid, the specific term "benefactor" in the reading refers to financial assistance, as it states "single largest financial benefactor."
Correct. The reading states, "Germany has become Ukraine's single largest financial benefactor," indicating a role as a major financial supporter.
Incorrect. While Germany is a strategic ally, the word "benefactor" in this specific context refers to financial contributions.

quiz.question: Which sentence from the news report effectively uses a participle clause to describe a consequence or simultaneous action?
options: Merz underscored Germany's position, asserting, 'Germany's security also depends on the outcome of this war.'

Video footage, independently verified, captured the moment an unmanned aerial vehicle crashed into the Pivnichyi Bridge as traffic moved across it, resulting in a large conflagration and a rising cloud of black smoke.
President Zelensky has consistently appealed to Western allies for more sophisticated military assistance, specifically requesting advanced interceptors.
option_feedback: Incorrect. This sentence uses a reporting verb "asserting" followed by a direct quote, not a participle clause indicating a consequence or simultaneous action of the main verb.
Correct. The phrase "resulting in a large conflagration" is a participle clause that clearly describes the consequence of the drone crash, directly following the main action.

Incorrect. While 'requesting' is a participle, this sentence structure primarily clarifies the appeal rather than describing a direct consequence or simultaneous action in the way the grammar point emphasizes.

quiz.question: What was the reported success rate of Ukraine's Air Force in intercepting Russian unmanned aerial vehicles?
options: Approximately 52 out of 135 were intercepted.
Around 125 out of 135 launched projectiles were shot down.
All jet-powered drones were successfully intercepted.
option_feedback: Incorrect. 52 was the number of jet-powered variants launched, not the total number intercepted.
Correct. The Air Force reported that "125 projectiles had been shot down" out of 135 launched overnight.
Incorrect. The report states 52 jet-powered ones were launched, but it doesn't confirm that all of them were shot down, only that 125 out of the total 135 were intercepted.

quiz.question: When the Russian foreign ministry warned foreign nationals to 'leave Kyiv,' what did they mean?
options: To register their presence with local authorities.
To temporarily relocate within the city.
To depart from the city.
option_feedback: Incorrect. 'Leave' means to depart from a place, not to register one's presence.
Incorrect. 'Leave' implies departing entirely, not just moving to a different part of the same location.
Correct. To 'leave' a place means to depart from it, indicating an instruction to exit Kyiv.

quiz.question: How does Russia attempt to justify its intensified attacks on Ukraine?
options: As a pre-emptive measure to prevent future Ukrainian offensives.
As retaliatory actions following Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy facilities.
As a strategy to dismantle Ukraine's military leadership.
option_feedback: Incorrect. The text does not mention pre-emptive measures; it explicitly frames the attacks as a "response" or "retaliatory actions" to specific Ukrainian actions.
Correct. The Russian defense ministry declared its intention to intensify its campaign "as a response to Zelensky's earlier remarks about escalating attacks on Russian oil refineries."
Incorrect. While military targets might be included, the explicit justification provided in the text is for "retaliatory attacks" against energy facilities.

quiz.question: The phrase "gaping hole" in the social media content description emphasizes what aspect of the damage?
options: The depth of the hole.
The unusual shape of the hole.
The large, wide-open nature of the damage.
option_feedback: Incorrect. While a gaping hole might be deep, the primary emphasis of "gaping" is on its wide-open characteristic, not depth.
Incorrect. The term "gaping" describes the size and openness, not necessarily an unusual or irregular shape.
Correct. "Gaping" specifically describes something that is wide open, highlighting the extensive and visually prominent nature of the damage to the traffic lane.

quiz.question: When the Russian foreign ministry 'reiterated' a warning, what does this imply about the warning?
options: It was a new warning issued for the first time.
It was a previous warning that was repeated.
It was a warning that was unexpectedly withdrawn.
option_feedback: Incorrect. To 'reiterate' means to state or do again, implying it's not a new warning.
Correct. 'Reiterated' means to say something again or a number of times, typically for emphasis or clarity, indicating it's a repeated warning.
Incorrect. 'Reiterated' implies repetition, not withdrawal, of a statement.

news_brief_sentences: The latest Russian unmanned aerial vehicle attack on Kyiv's Pivnichyi (Northern) Bridge coincided with a surprise visit from German Chancellor Friedrich Merz to the Ukrainian capital.

Video footage, independently verified, captured the moment an unmanned aerial vehicle crashed into the Pivnichyi Bridge as traffic moved across it, resulting in a large conflagration and a rising cloud of black smoke.
This attack marked the fourth successive day that major bridges in Kyiv have been targeted by Russian aerial assaults, as Moscow ramps up attacks on critical infrastructure in Ukraine's capital.

Two individuals sustained non-fatal injuries when the Pivnichyi Bridge was struck for the second day in a row, with the Pivdennyi (Southern) Bridge also having been targeted multiple times earlier in the week.
Other social media content showed a gaping hole in the middle of a traffic lane on the bridge, evidencing significant structural damage.

Kyiv's eight bridges spanning the Dnipro River are essential arteries, linking the city's eastern and western sectors, with many of the capital's estimated three million inhabitants relying heavily on public transport and personal vehicles for daily transit.
Although the two targeted bridges remain structurally sound, the damage and subsequent traffic restrictions have at times led to widespread gridlock across parts of the capital.
A Kyiv resident conveyed the severity of the travel disruption, stating, "'To get from the left bank to the right one and back - it's just hell.'"

Repair teams are actively addressing the damage, and officials are exploring contingency measures like temporary pontoon bridges, ferry services, and even a river tunnel to ensure Kyiv remains connected.
Beyond the bridge attacks, other Russian aerial bombardments on Sunday damaged a heating main, causing a temporary hot water shortage in the Desnyanskyi district.
Additionally, Russian drones struck a warehouse in Sumy, claiming one life, as reported by President Zelensky.
Ukraine's Air Force reported that out of 135 unmanned aerial vehicles launched overnight by Russia, including 52 jet-powered variants, 125 projectiles were successfully intercepted.
As emergency services responded, German Chancellor Merz met President Zelensky in Kyiv, and they laid wreaths for Ukrainian soldiers killed in the war.
Merz reaffirmed Germany's support for Ukraine, stating, "'Ukraine is facing decisive weeks. That is why I travelled to Kyiv today with the message: You can rely on us.'"
Merz underscored Germany's position, asserting, "'Germany's security also depends on the outcome of this war. That is why we are helping out of our own self-interest as well.'"
Since Merz assumed the chancellorship in May 2025, Germany has become Ukraine's single largest financial benefactor.

President Zelensky has consistently appealed to Western allies for more sophisticated military assistance, specifically requesting advanced interceptors capable of shooting down newer jet-powered Russian unmanned aerial vehicles and ballistic missiles.
Russia's defense ministry declared its intention to intensify its campaign across Ukraine, framing it as a response to Zelensky's earlier remarks about escalating attacks on Russian oil refineries.
The Russian foreign ministry reiterated a warning for foreign citizens, including diplomats, to leave Kyiv.

Responding to this warning, EU ambassador Katarína Mathernová declared, "'The EU Delegation is staying. Threatening us will not stop Europe's support for Ukraine. It only reminds us why that support matters!'"
German ambassador to Ukraine, Boris Ruge, echoed this sentiment, stating, "'Amen - we're staying'."

Experts assess that while Russian aerial assaults are unlikely to demolish the bridges outright, sustained targeting risks forcing their closure and weakening their structural integrity, ultimately rendering them unusable.
sentence_evidence: The latest attack came as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz made a surprise visit to Kyiv in a show of support against Russia's continuing full-scale invasion.

Video footage of Sunday's strike, verified by the BBC, shows cars moving on Pivnichnyi Bridge as a drone crashes into it before exploding, creating a ball of fire. A cloud of black smoke can be seen rising above the bridge.
Major bridges in Kyiv have been hit by Russian drone strikes for four consecutive days, as Moscow ramps up attacks on critical infrastructure in Ukraine's capital.

Two people were injured when the Pivnichnyi (Northern) Bridge was struck on Sunday morning for the second day in a row, while the Pivdennyi (Southern) Bridge was hit multiple times earlier in the week.
Other videos and pictures have emerged on social media showing a gaping hole in the middle of a traffic lane on the bridge.

Kyiv's eight bridges across the wide Dnipro River link the western (right) and eastern (left) parts, and many of the capital's estimated three million residents rely heavily on the metro lines and trains to travel across the city.
The two struck bridges are still standing - but the damage and restrictions to traffic and public transport have caused gridlock in parts of the capital at times.
"To get from the left bank to the right one and back - it's just hell," Kyiv resident Roman told the BBC on Sunday.

Large numbers of commuters cross the river, especially on weekdays. Repair teams are working to fix the damage and officials say they are planning temporary pontoon bridges, ferry services and even a tunnel under the river to keep Kyiv connected.
Klitschko also said a separate Russian drone strike had damaged a heating main, adding that there would be a temporary lack of hot water in the north-eastern Desnyanskyi district as a result.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenksy said on Sunday morning Russian drones had also attacked a warehouse in the north-eastern region of Sumy, killing one person.
Ukraine's Air Force said that overnight Russia had launched 135 drones, including 52 jet-powered ones. It said that 125 projectiles had been shot down.
As emergency services responded to the incidents, Germany's Merz met Zelenksy in Kyiv. They laid wreaths to Ukrainian soldiers who have been killed in the war.
Merz reaffirmed his country's support for Ukraine, writing on X: "Ukraine is facing decisive weeks. That is why I travelled to Kyiv today with the message: You can rely on us.
"Germany's security also depends on the outcome of this war. That is why we are helping out of our own self-interest as well."
Since Merz became chancellor in May 2025, Germany has become the single largest donor to Ukraine.

The Ukrainian president has made repeated appeals for Western allies to provide more military support to the country, including supplying advanced interceptors that can shoot down new jet-powered Russian drones and also ballistic missiles.

The Russian defence ministry said on Sunday it would intensify its strikes across Ukraine in response to comments made by Zelensky earlier this week, in which he said Kyiv would ramp up its attacks on Russian oil refineries.
The Russian foreign ministry on Saturday repeated a warning for foreign citizens, including diplomats, to leave Kyiv.

Responding to the warning, EU ambassador Katarína Mathernová wrote on X on Sunday: "The EU Delegation is staying. Threatening us will not stop Europe's support for Ukraine. It only reminds us why that support matters!"
German ambassador to Ukraine, Boris Ruge, reacted to Mathernova's post with: "Amen - we're staying".
Experts say Russian drones are unlikely to bring down the bridges - but repeated attacks will force their closure and risk weakening their structure, making them unusable.
